solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique after crossings); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Herb, in charge of a building in Rome

parts.note: basil is a culinary herb

explanation.surface: A herb-growing official runs some building in Rome.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is a building type that takes its name from Roman public halls; St Peter's in Rome is the most famous one.
explanation.definitionFit: A basilica is a large church or Roman public hall, the classic grand building of Rome.

clue.text: Spy almost fell from the sky, getting injured

indicators.note: almost means the word is cut just short of its final letter

parts.note: taken as written, then shortened
rain is what falls from the sky, so it rained

explanation.surface: A spy tumbles out of the sky, perhaps from a plane, and is hurt.
explanation.definitionFit: A sprained ankle or wrist is an injured one, hurt by a wrenched ligament.

clue.text: Generous family with daughter

parts.note: kin means relatives or family
D is the genealogical abbreviation for daughter

explanation.surface: A generous household that includes a daughter.
explanation.definitionFit: A kind person is giving and considerate, which is what generous means here.

clue.text: Tolerate hairstyle — one time!

parts.note: a perm is a permanent wave hairstyle
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: Putting up with a perm, just this once.
explanation.definitionFit: To permit something is to allow it, which is to tolerate or put up with it.

clue.text: Look hard for missing English celebrity

indicators.note: for missing says the word that follows is to be left out of the stare

parts.note: to stare is to look hard

explanation.surface: Scanning the room for a famous English person who has gone missing.
explanation.definitionFit: A star is a famous performer, the same as a celebrity.

clue.text: Faithful servant's last regret

indicators.note: last points to the final letter of the word servant's

parts.note: to rue is to regret

explanation.surface: A loyal servant's dying regret.
explanation.walkthrough: The apostrophe s is not a letter, so the final letter of servant's is T.
explanation.definitionFit: True can mean loyal and steadfast, as in a true friend.

clue.text: Jewel I perhaps must change

indicators.note: change tells you to alter the order of the letters before it

explanation.surface: Someone thinking that perhaps they must change their jewellery.
explanation.definitionFit: A sapphire is a precious gemstone, usually blue, so it is an example of a jewel.

clue.text: Conservative yarn, not the first

indicators.note: not the first says the opening letter of the word is dropped

parts.note: a yarn is a tall tale or story

explanation.surface: A rambling tale told by a Conservative politician.
explanation.definitionFit: Tory is the everyday name for a member of the UK Conservative Party.

clue.text: Award — ridicule also

parts.note: to rib someone is to tease or ridicule them
and adds one thing to another, meaning also

explanation.surface: Someone receiving an honour and being mocked as well.
explanation.definitionFit: A riband is a ribbon worn as a badge of honour, so a form of award, as in the Blue Riband.

clue.text: A crime to send back racehorse

indicators.note: send back asks for the horse's name to be read from right to left

parts.note: Red Rum was the famous racehorse that won the Grand National three times

explanation.surface: A crime story about returning a racehorse to its stable.
explanation.walkthrough: Red Rum is the celebrated horse that won Britain's Grand National steeplechase three times in the 1970s.
explanation.definitionFit: Murder is the unlawful killing of a person, the gravest example of a crime.

clue.text: Twelve? I had nine initially in force

indicators.note: in places the shorter pieces within the word for force

parts.note: might means power or force
I'd is the contraction of I had

indicators.note: initially picks the opening letter of nine

explanation.surface: Someone asked about twelve says they first had nine on the team in force.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Twelve?' looks like a number to be used in wordplay, but it is the definition: the hour.
explanation.definitionFit: Midnight is twelve o'clock at night, so twelve names that hour on the clock.

clue.text: That woman turned up in picture house

indicators.note: in a down entry, turned up means the letters read from bottom to top
in says the letters sit inside the words picture house

parts.note: the letters run across the end of picture into house

explanation.surface: A woman appears unexpectedly at the cinema.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Picture house' is an old name for a cinema, but here it just supplies hidden letters: REH, reading up the grid.
explanation.definitionFit: Her is the object pronoun for a female person, so it stands for that woman.

clue.text: Some fancy a new colour

indicators.note: Some says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Some people would like a new colour scheme.
explanation.definitionFit: Cyan is a greenish-blue shade, one of the printing primaries, so it is a colour.

clue.text: Public officials love getting into awkward situations

indicators.note: getting into puts one piece inside the other

parts.note: to be in a corner is to be in an awkward situation
love is zero in tennis, which looks like O

explanation.surface: Officials whose love affairs land them in tight spots.
explanation.definitionFit: Coroners are officials who hold inquests into unexplained deaths, appointed public office holders.

clue.text: Rubs lady in need of massage, ridiculously

indicators.note: massage works the letters over, kneading them into a fresh order

explanation.surface: A masseur rubs a lady who badly needs a massage.
explanation.definitionFit: Absurdly and ridiculously are synonymous adverbs, both meaning in a laughable or senseless way.

clue.text: Eccentric person, one bearing greetings?

definitions.meaning: first meaning: an odd or amusing character
second meaning: a greetings ... carries a message such as a birthday wish

explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags that the second definition is playful: a card bears greetings rather than a person.
explanation.definitionFit: The word is informal for a comic eccentric and also the folded item sent on birthdays.

clue.text: Unpoetic stuff about border plant

indicators.note: about means the first piece goes round the second

parts.note: prose is writing that is not verse
a rim is an edge or border

explanation.surface: Plain writing about a flower border.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Border plant' reads as one phrase about a garden; the definition is just plant.
explanation.definitionFit: The primrose is a pale yellow spring-flowering wild plant.

clue.text: Flaps from article appearing in illustrations

indicators.note: appearing in puts the article inside the word for illustrations

parts.note: pics is short for pictures, illustrations
an is the indefinite article

explanation.surface: Worries prompted by an article with pictures.
explanation.definitionFit: A flap is an informal word for a state of agitation, so flaps are panics.

clue.text: Longed, desperately, to be prosperous

indicators.note: desperately suggests wild agitation, so the letters are thrown into disorder

explanation.surface: Someone yearned hard to become wealthy.
explanation.definitionFit: Golden can mean flourishing or thriving, as in a golden age, so prosperous.

clue.text: Instrument for blokes, oddly unused

indicators.note: oddly unused means the odd-numbered letters are discarded, keeping the even ones

explanation.surface: A musical instrument meant for men that oddly goes unplayed.
explanation.walkthrough: The letters start in 'for', not 'blokes': drop f, r, b, l, k, s and O, B, O, E remain.
explanation.definitionFit: The oboe is a double-reed woodwind instrument.

clue.text: Aristocrat from this country cutting half of debt

indicators.note: cutting means the country's letters slice into the other piece
half of keeps the first two of the four letters of debt

parts.note: for a British setter this country is the UK

explanation.surface: A nobleman from Britain who has written off half of what he is owed.
explanation.walkthrough: The Times is a British paper, so 'this country' is the UK.
explanation.definitionFit: A duke is the highest rank of British peer, so a titled aristocrat.

clue.text: Preserve a track for singer in cage?

parts.note: to can food is to preserve it in tins
RY is the abbreviation for railway, a track

explanation.surface: Instructions to save a racetrack for a performer who feels caged.
explanation.definitionFit: Canaries are songbirds traditionally kept in cages as pets; the question mark flags the description.

clue.text: Jersey, possibly, with large hood

parts.note: a Jersey is a breed of cow, so an example of a cow
L is the clothing-size abbreviation for large

explanation.surface: A sweater, maybe, with a big hood.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Jersey' suggests a sweater, which fits a hood; it is really the dairy cattle breed from the Channel Island of Jersey.
explanation.definitionFit: A cowl is a loose hood, especially one on a monk's habit.

clue.text: Part of egg may go all black, finally

indicators.note: finally takes the closing letter of each of the four words that precede it

explanation.surface: An egg that has gone off may turn completely black at the end.
explanation.definitionFit: The yolk is the yellow central portion of an egg, surrounded by the white.

clue.text: Craven cold war moves by Yankee

indicators.note: moves suggests the letters shift position into a fresh order

parts.note: Y is Yankee in the NATO phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: Timid Cold War manoeuvres by the Americans.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Yankee' points to Americans in the Cold War, but here it is just the radio code word for Y.
explanation.definitionFit: Craven and cowardly are synonyms, both describing someone lacking courage.
